userStories.title: Shorthand and tier models keep their effort suffix
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve suffixed model selectors through their base alias or tier while preserving the selected effort on the dispatched model id.

**Motivation** — `resolveConfiguredModel` (`src/config/schema-types.ts`) looks up `MODEL_SHORTHAND_TIERS[selection.model.toLowerCase()]` on the whole string, so `sonnet[medium]` misses the `sonnet` -> `balanced` alias, falls through to the literal path and warns at every resolution (three times in one workflow run).

**Approach** — Split the effort suffix off with `parseModelSpec` (exported by `@nathapp/nax-agent`) before any alias or tier lookup, resolve the base, then put the suffix back on the resolved model id. The config-site suffix replaces any suffix the tier entry already carries.

`parseModelSpec(raw: string): ModelSpec` — `packages/nax-agent/src/cost/model-spec.ts`, exported from `@nathapp/nax-agent`; `ModelSpec` is `{ model: string; effort?: string }`. Only a well-formed trailing `[..]` is a suffix.

`MODEL_SHORTHAND_TIERS` (`haiku` -> `fast`, `sonnet` -> `balanced`, `opus` -> `powerful`), `resolveModelForAgent(models, agent, tier, defaultAgent): ModelDef`, `resolveTierMembership`, `resolveModel(entry: ModelEntry): ModelDef` — `src/config/schema-types.ts`.

`ModelDef` — `{ provider: string; model: string; pricing?; contextWindow?; env? }`.

`resolveConfiguredModel(models, preferredAgent, selection, defaultAgent): ResolvedConfiguredModel`
- Target: same signature; shorthand and tier lookups use the base from `parseModelSpec(selection.model)`; a resolved `modelDef.model` carries the selection's effort suffix when the selection had one.

`isUnrecognizedLiteralModel(model: string): boolean`
- Target: same signature; evaluates the base from `parseModelSpec(model)`, and returns `false` for a base that is a `MODEL_SHORTHAND_TIERS` key (case-insensitive).

A suffixed shorthand whose base is not a known alias or tier (`sonet[medium]`): Unchanged: resolves as a literal and warns.

Changes `resolveConfiguredModel` and `isUnrecognizedLiteralModel` so a model selector with a trailing `[effort]` resolves through the shorthand alias or tier of its base, with the suffix carried onto the resolved model id; `resolvePlanModelSelection` then keeps such a `plan.model` instead of falling back.

**Scope** — In: shared config resolution/recognition and the existing plan entry-point regression tests. Out: workflow publishing, ledger commits, final status and flagged-decision reporting (US-002–US-005); changes to the nax-agent parser. Validating effort values inside the suffix (`[ultra]` passes through unchanged, as today).

**Interface** — Preserve the existing signatures:
```typescript
resolveConfiguredModel(models, preferredAgent, selection, defaultAgent): ResolvedConfiguredModel
isUnrecognizedLiteralModel(model: string): boolean
parseModelSpec(raw: string): ModelSpec
```

**Implementation/test notes** — Keep bare string selectors, custom tier/default-agent membership and existing protocol-boundary warnings intact. Preserve all ModelDef metadata and avoid mutating configured object entries when replacing a suffix. Extend test/unit/config/schema-types.test.ts and test/unit/cli/plan-runtime.test.ts with failing cases first; no existing tests require expectation rewrites for this story. Exercise resolvePlanModelSelection itself, not only its imported guard, and collect logger entries to assert the exact warning behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] resolveConfiguredModel with models.claude = { fast: "claude-haiku-5", balanced: "claude-sonnet-5", powerful: "claude-opus-5" } and selection { agent: "claude", model: "sonnet[medium]" } returns modelTier: "balanced" and modelDef.model: "claude-sonnet-5[medium]".
[unit] With the same models, resolveConfiguredModel with selection { agent: "claude", model: "haiku[low]" } returns modelTier: "fast" and modelDef.model: "claude-haiku-5[low]".
[unit] With the same models, resolveConfiguredModel with selection { agent: "claude", model: "opus[high]" } returns modelTier: "powerful" and modelDef.model: "claude-opus-5[high]".
[unit] With the same models, resolveConfiguredModel with selection { agent: "claude", model: "Sonnet[high]" } returns modelTier: "balanced" and modelDef.model: "claude-sonnet-5[high]".

[unit] When models.claude.balanced is "claude-sonnet-5[high]", resolveConfiguredModel with selection { agent: "claude", model: "sonnet[low]" } returns modelDef.model: "claude-sonnet-5[low]" (the selection's suffix replaces the tier entry's).

[unit] When models.claude.balanced is "claude-sonnet-5[high]", resolveConfiguredModel with selection { agent: "claude", model: "sonnet" } returns modelDef.model: "claude-sonnet-5[high]" (no selection suffix leaves the entry's suffix in place).

[unit] When models.claude.balanced is the object { provider: "anthropic", model: "claude-sonnet-5", contextWindow: 200000 }, resolveConfiguredModel with selection { agent: "claude", model: "sonnet[medium]" } returns a modelDef with provider: "anthropic", contextWindow: 200000 and model: "claude-sonnet-5[medium]".
[unit] With the same claude models, resolveConfiguredModel with selection { agent: "claude", model: "balanced[high]" } returns modelTier: "balanced" and modelDef.model: "claude-sonnet-5[high]".

[unit] Resolving selection { agent: "claude", model: "sonnet[medium]" } logs no warn entry with the message "Configured model is neither a tier nor a recognizable model id — dispatching as a literal".
[unit] Resolving selection { agent: "claude", model: "sonet[medium]" } logs that warn message once, and returns modelTier: undefined and modelDef.model: "sonet[medium]".
[unit] isUnrecognizedLiteralModel("sonnet[medium]") returns false.
[unit] isUnrecognizedLiteralModel("sonet[medium]") returns true.
[unit] isUnrecognizedLiteralModel("claude-opus-5[high]") returns false.
[unit] isUnrecognizedLiteralModel("turbo[high]") returns true.

[unit] resolvePlanModelSelection with plan.model: { agent: "claude", model: "sonnet[high]" } and the claude models above returns modelTier: "balanced" and modelDef.model: "claude-sonnet-5[high]", and logs no "plan.model is neither a tier nor a recognizable model id" warning.

routing.reasoning: Small shared resolver/guard correction using an existing public parser, with metadata and plan-fallback regressions but no new abstraction.

suggestedCriteria: resolveConfiguredModel with a suffixed selection leaves the configured ModelDef object's original model value unchanged.

userStories.title: Add workflow.publish modes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let workflow callers choose PR publishing, push-only publishing or local-only completion without changing the default PR behavior.

**Motivation** — An orchestrator that opens the PR itself gets two PR attempts on one branch, and has no way to turn nax's off.

**Approach** — `workflow.publish` selects what `publish()` does after the final gates: `pr` (default, today's behaviour), `push` (push, wait for CI, open no PR, ask no approval; outcome `pushed`), `none` (no push, no PR; outcome `local-only`).

`WorkflowConfig` (`src/config/runtime-types-workflow.ts`) and `WorkflowConfigObjectSchema` (`src/config/schemas-workflow.ts`)
- Target: new optional field `publish?: WorkflowPublishMode`, where `type WorkflowPublishMode = "pr" | "push" | "none"`; the schema field is `z.enum(["pr", "push", "none"]).default("pr")`. Readers treat an absent value as `"pr"`.

`FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS` (`src/cli/config-descriptions.ts`) — new entry `"workflow.publish"` next to the other `workflow.*` keys, describing the three modes.

`FeatureOutcome` (`src/workflow/types.ts`)
- Target: `"ready" | "draft" | "local-only" | "pushed"`.

`publish(fc, input): Promise<PublishOutcome>` (`src/workflow/finalize.ts`)
- Target: same signature; branches on `fc.workflow.publish ?? "pr"` and runs the ledger commits below. Ledger implementation/calls are owned by US-003; this story establishes the final branching they attach to.

`isFinishedAtHead(prior, head)` (`src/workflow/feature.ts`, file-local)
- Target: also treats a prior with `outcome: "pushed"` at the same HEAD as finished.

`push` mode: `commitLedger -> push -> wait for CI`; no PR call, no `askApproval`, outcome `pushed`, `ci` from the wait, `reasons` from `readinessReasons` with the CI result plus the dirty-tree reason (the flagged count stays a reason). The commitLedger portion is US-003's contribution.

The `none` check runs first: on any branch, with or without a forge, `none` returns `local-only` with the single target reason `publish disabled (workflow.publish: none)` after the readiness and dirty-tree reasons.

`publish()` grows by two modes and the ledger calls; keep it under the complexity limits by extracting file-local helpers (for example one for the `push` branch and one fail-open wrapper around `_featureDeps.commitLedger` that logs and returns `false` on a throw). The ledger wrapper belongs to US-003.

Failure handling: `push` mode: the push fails — Outcome `local-only` with the `push failed: ...` reason, as in `pr` mode. `push` mode: run aborted during the CI wait — Throws `NaxError` `WORKFLOW_ABORTED`, as in `pr` mode. Preserve existing dry-run, non-feature-branch and no-forge local-only target behavior for pr/push.

**Scope** — In: config type/schema/defaults/descriptions, pushed outcome, publish mode branches and same-HEAD pushed skip. Out: ledger helper/commits (US-003), completion status (US-004), flagged-id reporting (US-005) and model resolution (US-001). Any advisor approval, PR, or PR promotion in `push` mode — the caller owns the PR. Re-running a feature whose prior run ended `local-only` (including `publish: "none"`) at the same HEAD — it runs the feature workflow again, as today. koda-side changes (nathapp-io/koda#270) and nax-finish skill support for the new `pushed` outcome.

**Interface**
```typescript
type WorkflowPublishMode = "pr" | "push" | "none";
publish?: WorkflowPublishMode;
publish(fc, input): Promise<PublishOutcome>
```

**Implementation/test notes** — Use _featureDeps for forge/push/CI/PR effects; a push uses commitAndPush(..., { skipCommit: true }). Keep readiness independent of feature passed. Extend finalize.test.ts with mode/absence/abort/error cases and assert forbidden calls explicitly. Own adding publish: pr to the expected object in test/unit/config/workflow-config.test.ts's defaults test while keeping every other default as asserted; own widening seedFinished.over.outcome in test/unit/workflow/feature.test.ts to include pushed, with existing callers unchanged. No newly created source files are required. US-003 depends on this story and adds the ledger calls to the branch structure established here.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] NaxConfigSchema.parse({}).workflow.publish equals "pr".
[unit] NaxConfigSchema.safeParse({ workflow: { publish: "push" } }) succeeds with workflow.publish "push", and the same for "none".
[unit] NaxConfigSchema.safeParse({ workflow: { publish: "draft" } }) fails.

[unit] publish with fc.workflow.publish "push" calls _featureDeps.commitAndPush with skipCommit: true and then _featureDeps.waitForChecks, and never calls `_featureDeps.openDraftFinishPr` or `_featureDeps.openOrPromotePr`.

[unit] publish with fc.workflow.publish "push" and a CI wait returning green returns outcome: "pushed", ci: "green", no url, and empty reasons when the record's final gates are green, reviewRan is true, every story is complete, nothing is flagged and the tree is clean.
[unit] publish with fc.workflow.publish "push" never asks the advisor: an advisor fake that records questions records none.

[unit] publish with fc.workflow.publish "push" and an uncommitted non-.nax file in the tree returns outcome: "pushed" with "uncommitted changes after the branch fix" in reasons.

[unit] publish with fc.workflow.publish "push" and input.flagged 2 returns "2 ruling(s) flagged for a human" in reasons.

routing.reasoning: The modes add bounded branches to existing push/CI/PR seams plus additive config/outcome fields and one skip predicate; existing fixtures support direct failing behavioral tests without a new integration abstraction.

modifiedFiles.reason: the test "defaults: pipeline mode, every workflow default filled (Zod 4 prefault)" asserts `parsed.workflow` equals an object without `publish`. Under US-002 the parsed defaults carry `publish: "pr"`; US-002 owns adding `publish: "pr"` to that expected object, keeping every other default as asserted.

the fixture helper `seedFinished` (line 77) types `over.outcome` as `"ready" | "draft" | "local-only"`, so the US-002 test of an already-finished `pushed` prior cannot be written against it. US-002 owns widening that parameter type to include `"pushed"`; existing callers are unchanged.

userStories.title: Commit and push the advisor ledger with the branch
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Ensure workflow publishing commits only the advisor decisions ledger and pushes approval decisions without letting ledger failures alter publishing outcomes.

**Motivation** — Nothing commits it, so every approved run leaves the ledger modified, and branch-scope rulings written at `adjudicate` after the last auto-commit miss the pushed branch.

**Approach** — A ledger-only commit (`git add` + `git commit --no-verify -- <ledger>`, message `chore(<feature>): advisor decisions`) runs before the first push and on every path that does not push, and again after the advisor's approval, followed by a second push when that commit was made. No `[skip ci]`: a skipped required check blocks a merge.

New: `commitLedger(projectDir: string, feature: string): Promise<boolean>` in `src/workflow/git.ts`, wired as `_featureDeps.commitLedger`; returns `true` only when it created a commit.

The pipeline-mode ledger commit to mirror: `commitLedger` in `src/finish/advise.ts` (`git add -- <path>`, `git diff --cached --quiet -- <path>`, `git commit --no-verify -m "chore(<feature>): advisor decisions" -- <path>`).

`ledgerPath(repoRoot, feature): string` — `src/advisor/ledger.ts`; resolves `.nax/features/<feature>/decisions.jsonl`.

`commitAndPush(repoRoot, branch, message, opts: { skipHooks?; skipCommit?; excludeDir? })` — `src/finish/commit.ts`; throws `NaxError` `FINISH_GIT_PUSH_FAILED` on a failed push.

`_featureDeps` (`src/workflow/feature-deps.ts`): `detectForge`, `commitAndPush`, `openDraftFinishPr`, `openOrPromotePr`, `waitForChecks`. `_workflowDeps.git(args, cwd)` (`src/workflow/step-context.ts`).

`askApproval(advisor, { feature, evidence })` and `readinessReasons(facts)` — `src/workflow/approval.ts`.

**Ledger commit and publish order**

`pr` mode, forge present, publishable branch:
```
commitLedger -> push -> open draft PR -> wait for CI -> [askApproval
  -> commitLedger -> push again only if that commit was made] -> promote or keep the draft
```

`push` mode: `commitLedger -> push -> wait for CI`; no PR call, no `askApproval`, outcome `pushed`, `ci` from the wait, `reasons` from `readinessReasons` with the CI result plus the dirty-tree reason (the flagged count stays a reason).

`pr` mode with a deterministic readiness reason never asks the advisor, so no second ledger commit runs.

`none` mode, and every `local-only` path (no forge, a non-feature branch, a failed push): `commitLedger` runs, nothing is pushed. A dry run skips `commitLedger` along with every other git write. 

`publish()` grows by two modes and the ledger calls; keep it under the complexity limits by extracting file-local helpers (for example one for the `push` branch and one fail-open wrapper around `_featureDeps.commitLedger` that logs and returns `false` on a throw).

The `none` check runs first: on any branch, with or without a forge, `none` returns `local-only` with the single target reason `publish disabled (workflow.publish: none)` after the readiness and dirty-tree reasons. After `askApproval` (approved or held), the second ledger commit runs, because `askApproval` appends the `finish-approval` decision either way.

**Failure Handling**
- `commitLedger` throws (git missing, index locked): Logged at warn with `storyId: "_run"`; `publish` continues as if no commit was made (fail-open).
- The ledger file does not exist: `commitLedger` returns `false`; no commit, no error.
- The second push (after the approval ledger commit) fails: Logged at warn with `storyId: "_run"`; promotion still runs and the outcome is unchanged.

**Scope** — In: ledger-only git helper/seam, publish commit ordering, conditional second push and fail-open logging. Out: config/mode definition and pushed skip (US-002), final run status (US-004), flagged-id reporting (US-005), model resolution (US-001) and changes to pipeline-mode finish. `[skip ci]` (or any CI-skip marker) on ledger commits — a skipped required check blocks a merge. Waiting for the CI run that the post-approval ledger push triggers — the PR is promoted on the CI result observed before the approval.

**Interface**
```typescript
commitLedger(projectDir: string, feature: string): Promise<boolean>
publish(fc, input): Promise<PublishOutcome>
```

**Implementation/test notes** — Use repo-relative pathspecs derived from ledgerPath and _workflowDeps.git; missing/unchanged files return false, failed git operations throw to the publish wrapper. Keep unrelated staged and unstaged edits out of the commit. Drive publish through _featureDeps.commitLedger (not just a standalone wrapper). Own adding a commitLedger fake to finalize.test.ts wire() that records { name: "ledger" } and returns a configurable boolean (default true). Own updating happy path order to ledger, push, draft, ci, ledger, push, promote; local-only non-dry cases get one ledger each, dry run none; first-push failure gets ledger, push; CI abort gets ledger, push, draft, ci; extend any full sequences added by US-002 similarly. Support returns/errors separately for each ledger/push call and restore all seams after tests. Create git-ledger integration tests with real temporary repositories, and retain existing fixture behavior otherwise. Depends on US-002: the ledger calls attach to the `publish()` branch structure (`pr`/`push`/`none`) that US-002 establishes.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] In a temporary git repository with a committed .nax/features/f/decisions.jsonl, appending a line to it and calling commitLedger(repo, "f") returns true and creates exactly one commit with the message chore(f): advisor decisions whose only changed path is .nax/features/f/decisions.jsonl.
[integration] In the same setup with an unrelated modified tracked file, commitLedger(repo, "f") leaves that file modified and uncommitted.
[integration] commitLedger(repo, "f") returns false and creates no commit when decisions.jsonl has no changes.
[integration] commitLedger(repo, "f") returns false and does not throw when .nax/features/f/decisions.jsonl does not exist.
[unit] publish in pr mode calls _featureDeps.commitLedger before its first _featureDeps.commitAndPush call.

[unit] publish in pr mode, when the advisor approves and the second commitLedger call returns true, calls commitAndPush a second time with skipCommit: true before openOrPromotePr; the call order is ledger, push, draft, ci, ledger, push, promote.

[unit] publish in pr mode, when the advisor holds and the second commitLedger call returns true, calls commitAndPush a second time before openOrPromotePr is called with keepDraft: true.
[unit] publish in pr mode with a deterministic readiness reason (a gate-open story) calls commitLedger exactly once and commitAndPush exactly once.

[unit] publish in pr mode with the advisor approving and the second ledger commit made, when the second push throws, still calls openOrPromotePr with keepDraft: false and returns outcome: "ready", and logs a warn entry with storyId: "_run".
[unit] publish on a non-feature branch (main) calls commitLedger once and never calls commitAndPush.
[unit] publish with no forge detected calls commitLedger once and never calls commitAndPush.

routing.reasoning: Path-limited real git commits combine with multiple publish branches, advisor-side ledger writes and fail-open second-push ordering; requires both real repository and seam-driven orchestration tests.

suggestedCriteria: commitLedger(repo, "f") leaves an unrelated already-staged tracked change staged and excludes it from the ledger commit.
commitLedger(repo, "f") creates the ledger commit even when the repository's pre-commit hook would reject a normal commit.
publish in none mode returns the same local-only outcome and reasons when commitLedger throws, and logs a warn entry with storyId: "_run".

modifiedFiles.reason: `wire()` fakes every forge-side dep but not `_featureDeps.commitLedger`, so the real git would run against the fixture repo path. US-003 owns adding a `commitLedger` fake to `wire()` that records a `{ name: "ledger" }` call and returns a configurable boolean (default `true`), and updating the call-sequence assertions that the new ledger calls extend: the happy path (line 116) becomes ledger, push, draft, ci, ledger, push, promote; the local-only test "main, an empty branch, a dry run, or no forge" (line 157) expects one ledger call for each non-dry-run case and none for the dry run; the push-failure test (line 165) becomes ledger, push; the abort-during-CI test (line 214) becomes ledger, push, draft, ci; and any test added by US-002 that asserts a full call sequence gains the same ledger entries.

userStories.title: Make final run status honor the feature workflow
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist failed workflow completion honestly without changing pipeline mode or green-gate draft/local-only runs.

**Motivation** — Workflow mode never writes `postRun.finish`, so a caller that reads `status.json` the way it reads a pipeline run (koda's runner does) reports the run as completed.

**Approach** — After the end phase, a workflow-mode run whose feature workflow did not pass has its run status turned from `completed` into `failed`. A draft or local-only result with green gates stays `completed`, matching pipeline mode where a draft finish leaves `run.status: "completed"` and the detail lives in `postRun.finish`. The `status.json` workflow block carries `passed`.

`runEndPhase(options, deps): Promise<boolean | undefined>` — `src/execution/end-phase.ts`; returns `undefined` in pipeline mode, the feature result's `passed` in workflow mode, `false` when the feature workflow throws.

`runCompletionPhase(options)` — `src/execution/runner-completion.ts`; its `finishRun` calls `writeFinalFeatureStatus`, the run-end auto-commit, then `runEndPhaseReported`, and `persistFinishStatus` writes `status.json` (run and feature) afterwards.

`StatusWriter.setRunStatus(status)` — `src/execution/status-writer.ts`; the run status union is `"running" | "completed" | "failed" | "stalled" | "crashed" | "precheck-failed" | "cost-limit" | "aborted"`.

`StatusWriter` — new read-only getter `runStatus` returning the value last passed to `setRunStatus`.

New: `workflowFinalRunStatus(current: RunStatus | undefined, workflowPassed: boolean | undefined): RunStatus | undefined` in `src/execution/lifecycle/workflow-run-status.ts` (pure; `RunStatus` is the run status union above), called in `finishRun` right after `runEndPhaseReported` and before `persistFinishStatus`. The call site invokes `options.statusWriter.setRunStatus(next)` only when `next` differs from the writer's current `runStatus`, so pipeline mode and a passing workflow add no `setRunStatus` call (test writers built by `makeStatusWriter` mock `setRunStatus`, and assertions such as `toHaveBeenLastCalledWith("failed")` in `runner-completion-skip.test.ts` must keep holding). `runner-completion.ts` is 578 lines against the 600-line source limit, so the rule lives in the new module and the call site adds no more than 3 lines.

`WorkflowStatusBlock` (`src/execution/status-file.ts`)
- Target: adds `passed?: boolean` and `flagged?: string[]`. This story owns passed; flagged belongs to US-005.

`workflowStatusBlock(stories, step, rec?)` (`src/workflow/status-block.ts`)
- Target: `rec?: Pick<WorkflowFeatureRecord, "outcome" | "url" | "passed" | "flaggedDecisions">`; copies `passed` when defined and `flagged` when `flaggedDecisions` is non-empty. This story adds the passed projection; US-005 adds flaggedDecisions/flagged.

**Scope** — In: pure downgrade rule, getter, completion call site and optional workflow passed projection. Out: model resolution (US-001), publish branching/ledger behavior (US-002/US-003) and flagged-id projection/reporting (US-005). Writing `postRun.finish` in workflow mode — callers read `run.status` and the `workflow` block. Changing pipeline-mode run status, finish behaviour or `postRun` contents. The `run:completed` reporters and the on-complete hook, which still fire before the end phase with the stories-only status. Reporting `aborted` for an abort during the feature workflow — such a run reports `failed`. `status.json` showing `run.status: "completed"` while the feature workflow is still running; the downgrade to `failed` lands when the end phase finishes.

**Interface**
```typescript
workflowFinalRunStatus(current: RunStatus | undefined, workflowPassed: boolean | undefined): RunStatus | undefined
```

**Implementation/test notes** — Derive the helper's RunStatus type from the existing RunStateSnapshot["runStatus"] union (src/execution/status-file.ts); do not assume a named RunStatus export already exists. Only completed plus explicit false becomes failed; return every other current value unchanged, including undefined on mock writers. Use endReport.workflowPassed, not outcome/CI/reasons, and do not add a setter for unchanged values. Project false using an undefined check, not truthiness. Drive runCompletionPhase with a real StatusWriter and a fake handleRunCompletion/workflow as in the duration suite; read the persisted temporary status.json to verify failed/green/throw cases. Add pure helper cases in lifecycle/workflow-run-status.test.ts and completion cases in runner-completion-workflow-status.test.ts. Own adding passed: true to feature.test.ts's already-finished done-block expected value; its seedFinished prior already carries true. Preserve runner-completion-skip mock assertions. Both normal sink.step and already-finished skip must continue to use workflowStatusBlock.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] workflowFinalRunStatus("completed", false) returns "failed".
[unit] workflowFinalRunStatus("completed", true) returns "completed".
[unit] workflowFinalRunStatus("completed", undefined) returns "completed".
[unit] workflowFinalRunStatus(undefined, false) returns undefined.
[unit] workflowFinalRunStatus("cost-limit", false) returns "cost-limit", and workflowFinalRunStatus("failed", false) returns "failed".

userStories.title: List flagged advisor rulings at run end
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Collect trusted human-confirmation decision ids after publishing and surface them in the persisted feature record, status and every run-end presentation.

**Motivation** — When the feature ends `local-only`, `deliverHeadsUp` returns `no-channel` and the end-of-run summary does not mention the ruling, so a ruling that changed an acceptance criterion can go unnoticed.

**Approach** — After publish, the publish step collects the ids of trusted ledger decisions with `needsHumanConfirm: true`, stores them on the feature record, and every surface built from the record shows them: `result.json`, the `status.json` workflow block, the end-of-run summary log line and the headless footer (with the hint `nax advisor list -f <feature>`).

`readTrustedDecisions(repoRoot, feature, outputDir): Promise<AdviceDecision[]>` — `src/advisor/ledger.ts`. `AdviceDecision` has `id: string` and `needsHumanConfirm: boolean`.

`WorkflowFeatureRecord` (`src/workflow/types.ts`) — new optional field `flaggedDecisions?: readonly string[]`.

`FeatureSteps` (`src/workflow/feature-machine.ts`) — new optional step `flaggedDecisions?: () => Promise<readonly string[]>`, wired in `buildFeatureEnv` (`src/workflow/feature-env.ts`) to `_workflowDeps.readTrustedDecisions(fc.projectDir, fc.feature, fc.outputDir)` (the same seam `finalize.ts` uses) filtered to `needsHumanConfirm === true`, in ledger order.

`WorkflowStatusBlock` (`src/execution/status-file.ts`)
- Target: adds `passed?: boolean` and `flagged?: string[]`. US-004 owns passed; this story adds flagged.

`workflowStatusBlock(stories, step, rec?)` (`src/workflow/status-block.ts`)
- Target: `rec?: Pick<WorkflowFeatureRecord, "outcome" | "url" | "passed" | "flaggedDecisions">`; copies `passed` when defined and `flagged` when `flaggedDecisions` is non-empty.

`WorkflowSummaryView` (`src/log-format/types.ts`) — new optional field `flagged?: { ids: readonly string[]; hint: string }`.

`buildWorkflowRunSummary(result, timing, feature?: string)` (`src/workflow/run-summary.ts`) — new optional third parameter used for the hint; `readWorkflowRunSummary(projectDir, feature, runId, timing)` forwards its `feature` argument to it.

Failure handling: `flaggedDecisions` step throws (unreadable ledger) — Logged at warn with `storyId: "_run"`; the record gets no `flaggedDecisions`; publish outcome unaffected.

The `flaggedDecisions` step (new) is invoked from the feature machine's publish step — drive `runFeatureMachine` from the `publish` step with a stubbed step and assert the persisted record, and drive `buildFeatureEnv` against a real ledger for the wiring. `WorkflowStatusBlock.passed` (US-004) and `.flagged` (US-005) are produced by `workflowStatusBlock`, which the feature env's `sink.step` and `runWorkflowFeature`'s already-finished skip both call.

**Scope** — In: optional step/record/view fields, post-publish collection, trusted feature-wide ledger read, result.json/status projections, summary log and footer rendering. Out: publish/ledger mechanics (US-002/US-003), final run status rule (US-004) and model resolution (US-001). Routing feature-scope (`_run`) advisor heads-ups through the story heads-up queue — the optional half of nax#2480; this spec only lists flagged rulings at run end. Per-run scoping or confirmation tracking of flagged decisions — the list is every trusted decision in the feature's ledger with `needsHumanConfirm: true`, across all runs of the feature. Flagged ids for a run that skips the feature workflow as already finished at the same HEAD — its `result.json` has no feature record, so the end-of-run summary shows no flagged list (the status block, built from the prior record, still carries it).

**Interface**
```typescript
flaggedDecisions?: readonly string[];
flaggedDecisions?: () => Promise<readonly string[]>;
flagged?: { ids: readonly string[]; hint: string };
buildWorkflowRunSummary(result, timing, feature?: string)
```

**Implementation/test notes** — Collect only after env.steps.publish completes, including pr/push/none/local-only outcomes; preserve existing passed/CI/outcome/reasons/head logic. No step means no record field. Read failure warns once and cannot prevent step: done. Persist flags through the existing sink.update to featureWorkflow.flaggedDecisions before done status projection. Do not read raw JSONL or add alternate trust logic: reuse readTrustedDecisions, including its existing audit-artifact checks, and preserve every trusted flagged decision across all runs in ledger order. Verify buildFeatureEnv wiring using both stubbed returns and real matching audit artifacts. Extend summary construction to emit flagged only for a nonempty list, with hint nax advisor list -f <feature> or nax advisor list when the optional argument is absent; ready outcomes must show flags just like local-only. formatWorkflowSummary adds a line containing Flagged for a human:, comma-separated ids and hint; summaryLine adds flagged <count> (<hint>) to the Workflow summary: info line. Reuse the view passed to the footer rather than rereading the ledger there. Existing records/fixtures lack flaggedDecisions and their assertions must remain unchanged. Tests exercise machine ordering/failure, env persistence, status projection, summary builder, renderer and reportWorkflowRun reading result.json; create feature-flagged-decisions.test.ts for the new machine/env regressions. Depends on US-003 and US-004: US-003 so the collected ids include the post-approval `finish-approval` decision, and US-004 because both stories extend `workflowStatusBlock`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] The feature env built by buildFeatureEnv, with _workflowDeps.readTrustedDecisions stubbed to return decisions D-1 (needsHumanConfirm: true), D-2 (false) and D-3 (true), resolves steps.flaggedDecisions() to ["D-1", "D-3"].
[unit] steps.flaggedDecisions() resolves to [] when _workflowDeps.readTrustedDecisions resolves to [].
[unit] runFeatureMachine started at the publish step, with a flaggedDecisions step resolving ["D-1"], ends with a record whose flaggedDecisions is ["D-1"], and calls flaggedDecisions after publish.

[unit] runFeatureMachine started at the publish step, with a flaggedDecisions step that rejects, ends with step: "done", the publish outcome recorded, no flaggedDecisions on the record, and one warn entry with storyId: "_run".
[unit] runFeatureMachine started at the publish step with no flaggedDecisions step ends with no flaggedDecisions on the record.
[unit] The record persisted to result.json by the feature env's sink.update after that publish step carries featureWorkflow.flaggedDecisions ["D-1"].
[unit] workflowStatusBlock(stories, "done", { outcome: "local-only", flaggedDecisions: ["D-1", "D-3"] }) returns a block with flagged: ["D-1", "D-3"].
[unit] workflowStatusBlock(stories, "done", { outcome: "ready", flaggedDecisions: [] }) returns a block without a flagged key.

[unit] buildWorkflowRunSummary(result, timing, "f") for a result whose feature record has outcome: "local-only" and flaggedDecisions: ["D-1"] returns flagged: { ids: ["D-1"], hint: "nax advisor list -f f" }.
[unit] buildWorkflowRunSummary(result, timing, "f") for a record with outcome: "ready" and flaggedDecisions: ["D-2"] also returns flagged with ids ["D-2"].
[unit] buildWorkflowRunSummary(result, timing) with no feature argument returns the hint "nax advisor list" for a non-empty list.
[unit] buildWorkflowRunSummary returns no flagged key when the record has no flaggedDecisions.

[unit] `formatWorkflowSummary` for a view with `flagged: { ids: ["D-1", "D-3"], hint: "nax advisor list -f f" }` includes a line containing "Flagged for a human:", the joined string "D-1, D-3" and "nax advisor list -f f".

[unit] reportWorkflowRun for a run whose result.json record has flaggedDecisions: ["D-1"] logs the Workflow summary: info line containing flagged 1 (nax advisor list -f <feature>) with the run's feature name.

routing.reasoning: Injected machine collection must propagate an optional record field through persistence, status, a shared summary view and two presentation surfaces without changing trust or legacy outputs.

suggestedCriteria: buildFeatureEnv steps.flaggedDecisions() reading a real ledger returns only needsHumanConfirm: true decisions with matching trusted audit artifacts, preserving their ledger order.
buildWorkflowRunSummary returns no flagged key when featureWorkflow.flaggedDecisions is an empty array.
runFeatureMachine at publish records flagged decision ids for outcome: "pushed" as well as ready, draft and local-only.
runWorkflowFeature's already-finished skip emits the prior feature record's nonempty flaggedDecisions in the done workflow status block.

analysis:
Existing-code enhancement covering nax#2499, #2508, #2507 and #2480. All implementation changes belong to packages/nax; packages/nax-agent is read-only context for its existing public parseModelSpec export. No new runtime dependency, package release, external orchestrator change or persisted-data migration is required. Done means suffixed aliases resolve without spurious fallback, callers can own publishing, the advisor ledger travels with the branch, final workflow failure is reflected in persisted run status, and flagged trusted decision ids reach every run-end reporting surface.

Architecture and constraints: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:15 establishes injected _deps for external calls; :130 gives the 600-line source hard limit, 30-line function target/50-line hard maximum, and 800-line test hard limit. Follow package Bun/TypeScript/bun:test conventions, shared @test/helpers fixtures, structured logging and conventional commits. Use existing seams rather than real network calls or monkey-patched globals. Read the index and relevant focused conventions before implementation. Scope is orchestration, not the agent's permission, credential or session contract.

US-001: packages/nax/src/config/schema-types.ts:168 defines haiku/sonnet/opus tier aliases; :185 performs fallback-inclusive tier membership; :194 treats unqualified unknown provider ids as unrecognized; :207 resolves configured selections, currently looking up the whole object selector string at :222 and :232. String selectors already use tier resolution at :214 and must retain their established semantics. packages/nax-agent/src/cost/model-spec.ts:31 uses a strict whole-string regex for a nonempty model and trailing nonempty bracket suffix, preserving malformed strings. Parse the object selector before alias/membership checks, preserve the resolved ModelDef's provider/pricing/contextWindow/env, and override only its model suffix when effort was explicitly selected; avoid mutating shared object entries returned directly by resolveModel. packages/nax/src/cli/plan-runtime/index.ts:30 delegates to resolveConfiguredModel and :40 falls back only for unresolved literals, so correcting the shared resolver/guard should eliminate the plan fallback without duplicating parsing there. Consumers include config barrels (packages/nax/src/config/index.ts:84, :89; types.ts:73; schema.ts:81), operations dispatch (packages/nax/src/operations/call-dispatch-prologue.ts:122) and model-preview helpers. Existing regression suites are packages/nax/test/unit/config/schema-types.test.ts:183 and :319 and packages/nax/test/unit/cli/plan-runtime.test.ts:15 and :168; retain custom tiers, default-agent fallback and protocol-boundary warnOnce behavior. The spec explicitly identifies no existing suffixed-alias assertions to modify.

US-002: packages/nax/src/config/runtime-types-workflow.ts:25 owns WorkflowConfig; packages/nax/src/config/schemas-workflow.ts:11 owns its Zod object and :32 derives WORKFLOW_DEFAULTS from parsing, with nested prefault defaults. Add an optional typed publish field and enum default pr so legacy hand-built configs and old config files retain the PR path. Check package config type barrels when exposing WorkflowPublishMode (packages/nax/src/config/index.ts:46). packages/nax/src/cli/config-descriptions.ts:64-80 is the workflow description group. packages/nax/src/workflow/types.ts:129 owns FeatureOutcome, used by record/result/PR-body and returned feature types; log-format/status outcome fields already accept string. packages/nax/src/workflow/finalize.ts:185 is publish: readiness and dirty reasons are assembled before target discovery, push, draft, CI and conditional approval. :52 guards dry run/protected branches/no forge, :59 performs skipCommit pushes and fail-open first-push fallback; :129 excludes nax-owned files through listUncommitted in packages/nax/src/workflow/git.ts:26. Check none before target discovery so it never detects a forge and has only the disabled target reason, following readiness/dirty reasons, even on main. Share CI wait/abort behavior with push mode without executing PR body/PR/approval operations. packages/nax/src/workflow/approval.ts:30 supplies deterministic reasons (CI pending is not blocking); :44 computes feature passed from stories/gates rather than publish readiness. packages/nax/src/workflow/feature.ts:101 only skips ready/draft priors at identical HEAD; add pushed but not local-only. Existing tests: packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/finalize.test.ts:55 wire fakes; :112 happy path; :150 local-only; :214 CI abort. US-002 owns adding publish: pr to the exact defaults assertion in packages/nax/test/unit/config/workflow-config.test.ts:7 and widening seedFinished's outcome parameter in packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/feature.test.ts:77. Old configuration has no migration step; pr remains the default and pipeline execution is unaffected.

US-003: add commitLedger to existing packages/nax/src/workflow/git.ts and inject it through packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-deps.ts:6. Git calls must use _workflowDeps.git, and ledgerPath comes from packages/nax/src/advisor/ledger.ts:30. Mirror the pipeline's path-limited add/diff/commit shape at packages/nax/src/finish/advise.ts:226, but return a boolean and gracefully handle a missing file. Distinguish git diff exit 1 (changed) from errors; no commit for clean/missing ledger; no broad add/commit, no CI-skip marker, and no unrelated tracked or staged path in the ledger commit. The helper's failures propagate to a publish-level warn/fail-open wrapper. Commit before the first push and on local-only/none paths, skip all writes for dry run, then commit again after any attempted approval, including held approval. Only a created second commit triggers a second skipCommit push; second-push failure warns and cannot undo the approval/promotion outcome. No new CI wait after that push. The feature machine reads HEAD after publish at packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-machine.ts:318, which captures the ledger commit for resume detection. packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/git.test.ts:22 demonstrates real temporary repositories; place new ledger-only git integration cases in test/integration/workflow/git-ledger.test.ts and reuse shared temp helpers. Update wire() in packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/finalize.test.ts:55 to fake commitLedger, default true, record ledger calls and permit per-call returns/errors; otherwise tests would run real git against /repo. Update all affected index-based/full call-order assertions, not just new tests.

US-004: packages/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-completion-phases.ts:410 writes final stories-only status via setRunStatus at :427. packages/nax/src/execution/runner-completion.ts:485 finishRun writes that status, stops heartbeat, repairs run state, auto-commits, then runs runEndPhaseReported at :556. The existing runner-completion.ts is 578 lines; do not expand it with a status matrix. packages/nax/src/execution/end-phase.ts:109 returns workflow result passed, :128-144 maps throws/CI-wait abort to false, :147 returns undefined for pipeline mode. Preserve every current status except completed+false, and never call setRunStatus for an unchanged result. packages/nax/src/execution/status-writer.ts:78 holds _runStatus initialized to running and :134 stores setter values; add a read-only getter over that state. Tests using makeStatusWriter have a mock setter that does not update state (packages/nax/test/helpers/status-writer.ts:45), so an undefined current value must stay undefined and cause no added setter call. Use a real writer to verify actual persisted JSON, following packages/nax/test/unit/execution/runner-completion-finish.test.ts:30 and the fake completion/workflow pattern in runner-completion-workflow-duration.test.ts:90. Preserve the existing runner-completion-skip last-setter regressions. packages/nax/src/execution/status-file.ts:27 and packages/nax/src/workflow/status-block.ts:5 need optional passed projection with explicit undefined checks to preserve false. Both buildFeatureEnv sink.step (packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-env.ts:89) and the already-finished path (packages/nax/src/workflow/feature.ts:114) use that projection. US-004 owns adding passed: true to the existing done-block assertion at packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/feature.test.ts:166. Green gates plus draft/local-only remain completed; publish outcome and CI readiness must not become run failure criteria. Reporters/hooks and postRun remain unchanged.

US-005: add optional record/step/view fields, with no eager defaults on legacy fixtures. packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-machine.ts:31 defines injected FeatureSteps; :315 publishStep currently records publish outcome/head/passed, and :344 persists each patch via sink.update before emitting done status. Collect flagged ids after publishing so the just-written finish-approval decision is included. Failure to read flags must warn once with storyId _run, leave the field absent and still finish/persist publishing. packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-env.ts:60 wires steps and :85 persists records to result.json through upsertFeatureRecord. Use its existing _workflowDeps.readTrustedDecisions(fc.projectDir, fc.feature, fc.outputDir), filter exactly needsHumanConfirm === true, preserve ledger order and include all feature runs. packages/nax/src/advisor/ledger.ts:106-133 verifies external audit artifacts and exact decision equality; reuse that trust boundary, do not replace it with plain readDecisions or raw JSONL. Verify buildFeatureEnv with both a stubbed seam and an actual ledger with matching audit artifacts. packages/nax/src/workflow/run-summary.ts:43 builds the view from featureWorkflow; :69 reads the per-run result. Pass optional feature through that chain and emit flagged only for nonempty ids, independently of publish outcome; use the bare nax advisor list hint when feature is absent. packages/nax/src/log-format/types.ts:76 owns WorkflowSummaryView; packages/nax/src/log-format/workflow-summary.ts:31 renders the footer; packages/nax/src/execution/workflow-end-report.ts:33 logs summaryLine and :42 forwards the same view to reporting; headless-formatter consumes the view, so do not duplicate ledger reads there. Relevant suites already exist at test/unit/workflow/feature-machine.test.ts, feature-env.test.ts, run-summary.test.ts, test/unit/log-format/workflow-summary.test.ts and test/unit/execution/workflow-end-report.test.ts. Use a separate feature-flagged-decisions.test.ts for new machine/env persistence regressions if needed to keep existing files bounded. No existing fixtures have flaggedDecisions, so absent/empty lists must add no output key and leave their assertions unchanged. Already-finished skips project prior record flags into status but have no feature record in this run's result/summary.

Dependency reconciliation: US-003 -> US-002; US-005 -> US-003, US-004; others none (hand-fixed after nax plan to match the spec).

Main risks: accidentally changing bare-tier/fallback resolution or mutating configured ModelDef objects; detecting forge in none mode; accidentally asking approval/creating PR in push mode; committing unrelated index entries; treating ledger failure as a publish failure; second push changing the recorded CI outcome; status mocks receiving extra setter calls or terminal statuses being downgraded; false passed disappearing; empty flags altering old JSON snapshots; collecting only current-run or untrusted decisions; resume behavior accidentally skipping local-only. Mitigate through exact behavioral tests at the real entry points, per-test seam restoration, real temporary git and status-file integration checks, and additive optional JSON fields. Run package-scoped targeted Bun tests during implementation (never bare bun test); automatic pipeline gates cover lint/typecheck/tests, and CI coverage remains a separate package gate. No generated AGENTS/CLAUDE/rules files need editing.

Refine self-audit: all 77 explicit spec acceptance criteria are retained in their original story (US-001: 15; US-002: 18; US-003: 16; US-004: 14; US-005: 14), including suffix-replacement/preservation parentheticals, clean-record qualifications, real-writer/faked-completion setup, default PR behavior and unchanged-outcome/last-setter regression anchors. Every criterion is observable through returns, thrown errors, injected-call traces, logs, git history or persisted JSON. All seven failure-table rows map to criteria: ledger throw US-003.16; missing ledger US-003.4; second push throw US-003.10; push-mode first push failure US-002.14; CI-wait abort US-002.16; flagged-step throw US-005.4; suffixed typo US-001.10. Each story already has negative-path and backward-compatibility criteria, so none were invented for the audit. All 14 feature-level exclusions remain verbatim, and each contextFiles array matches the spec's five recommended context files with no story output listed as input. Binding dependencies remain unchanged. Re-reading the current resolver, publish/machine/env seams, defaults and completion/writer code confirms the proposed changes attach to existing entry points. Clarified US-003's second-push-failure ready case with its approving-advisor/created-commit setup, without changing the expected outcome. Clarified that RunStatus derives from RunStateSnapshot["runStatus"] (packages/nax/src/execution/status-file.ts:290), rather than an existing named export. Reduced US-002 and US-004 to medium/tdd-simple: their existing seams and fixtures support bounded additive changes and direct regressions; US-003 retains complex routing for git/approval sequencing, and US-005 for persistence-to-multiple-surface integration. No acceptance criteria or feature exclusions were removed.
outOfScope: Routing feature-scope (`_run`) advisor heads-ups through the story heads-up queue — the optional half of nax#2480; this spec only lists flagged rulings at run end.
Per-run scoping or confirmation tracking of flagged decisions — the list is every trusted decision in the feature's ledger with `needsHumanConfirm: true`, across all runs of the feature.
`[skip ci]` (or any CI-skip marker) on ledger commits — a skipped required check blocks a merge.
Writing `postRun.finish` in workflow mode — callers read `run.status` and the `workflow` block.
Changing pipeline-mode run status, finish behaviour or `postRun` contents.
The `run:completed` reporters and the on-complete hook, which still fire before the end phase with the stories-only status.
Reporting `aborted` for an abort during the feature workflow — such a run reports `failed`.
Validating effort values inside the suffix (`[ultra]` passes through unchanged, as today).
Re-running a feature whose prior run ended `local-only` (including `publish: "none"`) at the same HEAD — it runs the feature workflow again, as today.
Any advisor approval, PR, or PR promotion in `push` mode — the caller owns the PR.
Waiting for the CI run that the post-approval ledger push triggers — the PR is promoted on the CI result observed before the approval.
`status.json` showing `run.status: "completed"` while the feature workflow is still running; the downgrade to `failed` lands when the end phase finishes.

Flagged ids for a run that skips the feature workflow as already finished at the same HEAD — its `result.json` has no feature record, so the end-of-run summary shows no flagged list (the status block, built from the prior record, still carries it).
koda-side changes (nathapp-io/koda#270) and nax-finish skill support for the new `pushed` outcome.
